RETURNS POLICY COST ANALYZER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

What do returns really cost your store?

Paste your orders — category, subtotal, amount refunded — and see what each return costs you, which categories lose money once returns are counted, and whether a return fee or restocking fee would pay.

Nothing is uploaded and no store is contacted. The text box is analysed in this browser and never leaves your device. Two behaviours — a fee talking buyers out of returning, and buyers leaving at checkout because of it — cannot be read from past orders, so you set them and the result shows how much they matter.

1. Paste your orders

2. What it found

By category, worst first

CategoryOrdersReturn rateReturns costMargin before → after

Every policy, against free returns

PolicyProfit vs nowPays when

Findings

RuleLevelDetail

Prefer a CLI, or want a CI check?

Same logic, zero dependencies, one command — reads a file or stdin:

node cli.mjs analyze orders.csv
cat orders.csv | node cli.mjs analyze -
node cli.mjs analyze orders.csv --margin 45 --out-ship 6.5 --resale 70 --days 90
node cli.mjs analyze orders.csv --deterrence 0.5 --drag 5 --json --fail-on warn

Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. More: What a return really costs, and when a return fee pays.

What's recognised

InputHandling

Deterrence and checkout drop-off are assumptions you set (defaults: a fee worth 10% of the order prevents 10% of its returns; 3% of buyers do not check out when a return fee worth 10% of the order is shown, more for bigger fees); exchanges, store credit, repeat purchases and lifetime value are not modelled; margin is the profit share of merchandise before shipping and fees.

Common questions

Does this connect to my store?

No. It reads the order rows you paste and never contacts Shopify, WooCommerce, Etsy, Amazon or any carrier. Every figure is arithmetic on your numbers plus two behaviours you set, so nothing here is a measurement of your customers.

How do I get the numbers?

Export orders from your store with the product category, the merchandise subtotal and the amount refunded. In Shopify the orders export carries Subtotal and Refunded Amount; the return label cost comes from your carrier report and is optional. Orders that were not returned get a refund of 0.

What counts as the cost of a return?

The outbound shipping you paid and cannot recover, the return label, the time to receive and inspect it, the share of returned goods you cannot resell, and the card fee, which processors generally keep when you refund. The margin on the sale is gone too, so a returned order is usually a loss, not a zero.

Would a return fee or restocking fee pay?

It depends on two things past orders cannot tell you: how many returns the fee talks buyers out of, and how many buyers it scares away at checkout. You set both, and the tool shows the drop-off at which each policy breaks even and the policy that loses least if your guesses are off.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The browser page runs on the text in your own browser and never sends it anywhere. The CLI reads a local file or stdin and makes no network call.

No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not financial, tax, legal or business advice. It does arithmetic on order rows you paste plus two behavioural assumptions you set; it is not a measurement of your customers and not a forecast of what a change will earn. Changing a returns policy changes what shoppers see and may be limited by consumer-protection law where you sell: check the rules for your market, try a change for a few weeks and compare conversion and return rate before keeping it. Shopify, WooCommerce and other store names are trademarks of their owners, used only to describe where numbers come from.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record. If a tool needs to survive, get cli.mjs and run it yourself.

Everything runs in your browser. The text you paste is never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (analyze_run, example_loaded) are counted only in local storage and can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

Related tools on the same repo: the Free Shipping Threshold Optimizer, the Bundle Discount Optimizer, the Shopify Fee Calculator and the Break-even ROAS Calculator.

Free and open source. If this saved you some guesswork, the code is under an MIT licence — support is entirely optional and never changes what the tool does.

returns-policy-guide.html.text:
Returns Policy Cost Analyzer

What a return really costs, and when a return fee pays

A refund looks like money handed back. It is more than that. Counting a return the way your books should:

  • The sale is gone. The margin you expected on the order is zero, not merely smaller.
  • Outbound shipping is sunk. You paid to send it and cannot get that back.
  • The return label if you offer free returns, plus handling to receive, inspect and restock.
  • Stock you cannot resell is written off at cost.
  • The card fee is generally not refunded by the processor.

Put numbers on those for your store, then rank product categories by what returns cost in total. The analyzer does that from an orders export, and tests seven return-fee and restocking-fee policies against free returns: the profit change at your assumptions, the checkout drop-off at which each breaks even, and the policy that loses least if you are wrong.

What does a return cost an online store?

More than the refund. You lose the margin on the sale, the outbound shipping, the return label, the time to receive and inspect the parcel, any stock you cannot resell, and usually the card fee, which processors keep.

Which products should I look at first?

Not the biggest sellers, the highest return categories weighted by their price. A category with a 35% return rate can show a healthy margin on the sales report and a thin or negative one once returns are counted. Paste orders by category and the tool ranks them by what returns cost.

Does a return fee reduce returns?

It can, mostly for low-conviction orders such as bracketing sizes, and it can also cost you buyers who read the policy and leave. Neither effect can be read from past orders, so the tool takes both as inputs and shows how the answer moves.

Are return fees allowed?

Rules differ by country and region, and some places guarantee a refund right for distance sales that limits what you can charge. This page is not legal advice: check the rules for the markets you sell into before changing a policy.

Next: paste your orders, or see the free shipping threshold optimizer for the other half of the checkout policy.

No warranty. Free and as-is, without warranty of any kind. Not financial, tax, legal or business advice; consumer-protection rules on returns differ by country and region. Arithmetic on numbers you provide plus assumptions you set, not a forecast of what a change will earn.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. Nothing you type is uploaded.
